dossier.public_summary: The 0.74-day dip sits on the M-dwarf itself, but its depth jumps from 9032 ppm to 522 ppm between sectors and even within the same pipeline, and the period exactly matches the star's 21,000-30,000 ppm spot modulation. The long duration is unphysical for this tiny star, so the signal is the star's own variability, not a planet.

reasons.why: Difference imaging over three sectors puts the dip on the M dwarf and >40 sigma from any neighbour that could fake it, so a blended eclipse is ruled out.
reasons.value: verdict: on_target offset_arcsec: 2.659 err_arcsec: 1.051 offset_sigma: 2.53 suspects 43-65.3 sigma away

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor ~17 between SPOC and QLP and even within SPOC (6381 vs 9032 ppm) with p_constant 1.982e-23 and 0.007 within SPOC, so the signal is not a steady transit.
reasons.value: p_constant: 1.982e-23 chi2: 108.8 dof: 3 depth_change_pct: 191.3 per_sector 6381,9032,1856,522 ppm

reasons.why: The change is real, not a pipeline offset, inconsistent with a planet on a fixed orbit.
reasons.value: verdict: changes_within_a_source SPOC p_constant: 0.007175958237815757 QLP p_constant: 0.09200769395159555

reasons.why: The detected period is exactly the star's rotation period (false_alarm: 0.0) with huge spot amplitudes, and phase_curve amplitude 8016 ppm ratio_to_depth 1.336 chi2 693.7 dof 9 indicates the out-of-transit swing is spot modulation, not a planet.
reasons.value: rotation_d: 0.743 signal_period_d: 0.743014 signal_over_rotation: 1.0000188425302825 amplitude_ppm: 21075 in sector 18, 29984 in sector 58

reasons.why: Duration for the TIC radius 0.254705 Rsun is 1.797x longer than central, requiring density far below stellar, so a single transit fit is unphysical.

V-shape is not significant and there is no secondary or odd-even difference, but alone a flat bottom and no binary sign do not prove a planet when centroid and rotation already identify the source as variability.
